
`bumpDocVersion` is the only store function that increments `docs.version`, and `bumpRuleVersion` the only one that increments `rules.version`. Edge tables hold current state only, for the hot path, so the bump is where history is written. In the caller's transaction, `bumpDocVersion` copies the pre-update `docs` row into `doc_versions`, the document's outgoing `doc_edges` into `doc_edge_versions` and its `doc_rules` into `doc_rule_versions`, all at the version being replaced, then returns the next version. `bumpRuleVersion` copies the rule's outgoing `rule_edges` into `rule_edge_versions` at the replaced version, then inserts the next `rule_versions` row. A test fails the build on any other statement that increments either version column. Reading version N of a document, its edges or its arrangement reads the live tables when N is current and the snapshot tables otherwise. Diffing versions is out of scope.

A document's version moves when a plan or a draft spec has its body edited, when a revision lands, when an accepted document is amended in place, and when a plan's edges change. A draft body edit snapshots the text it replaces, so an overwritten draft stays readable through `lode doc versions` and `--if-version` can detect a second writer. A draft spec's edge writes change the live edges in place and keep its version.
